hypotheses.claim: ConstTag builds the derived via b.thunk (non-async arrow), so awaits inside {@const} in async mode end up in a non-async function; the correct path (used by $derived()) wraps init differently so awaits become async/deferred.
evidence_refs: compiled_client: `const number = $.derived(() => await Promise.resolve(5))` inside boundary
hypotheses.prediction: Changing ConstTag to build the derived the same way $derived() expressions do (so await is legal inside) makes the holdout test pass and render '5'.
hypotheses.falsifier: If create_derived/b.thunk is identical for both paths, the bug must be elsewhere (e.g. analyze phase marking expression as last-evaluated/reactive).

hypotheses.claim: AwaitExpression misclassifies await inside @const: is_reactive_expression/is_last_evaluated_expression fails, so it emits a bare await instead of the `$.save`-wrapped async pattern.
hypotheses.prediction: AwaitExpression should return b.call(b.await(b.call('$.save', argument))) for await inside @const; fixing classification compiles to legal async derived code.
hypotheses.falsifier: If the emitted form is already $.save-wrapped yet still non-async, the defect is in create_derived not making the function async.
